result.topic_en: Euler gives formulas for the Moon's apparent diameter and horizontal parallax at conjunction, opposition and quadrature, with values at apogee and perigee. He then sets up the Moon's true hourly motion from the differential equation for longitude and begins substituting numerical coefficients, each with its logarithm beneath.
result.transcription:
De diametris apparentibus motuque horario vero solis ac lunae, in eclipsibus lunaribus. 387

§. 8. Ex his ergo concludimus fore in conjunctione
\hfill in Apog. \quad in Perig.
diametrum lunae appar. $= 31'\,30'' - 122\cos v + 4\cos 2v$ \quad $29'\,32''$ \quad $33'\,36''$
parallaxin horizontalem $= 57\;\;8 - 222\cos v + 8\cos 2v$ \quad $53\;\;34$ \quad $60\;\;58$
in oppositione vero erit
diameter lunae app. $= 31\;\;32 - 122\cos v + 4\cos 2v$ \quad $29\;\;34$ \quad $33\;\;38$
parallaxis horiz. $= 57\;\;10 - 222\cos v + 8\cos 2v$ \quad $53\;\;36$ \quad $61\;\;0$
atque in quadraturis
diameter lunae app. $= 31\;\;3 - 83\cos v + \cos 2v + \cos V$ \quad $29\;\;41$ \quad $32\;\;27$
parallaxis horiz. $= 56\;\;18 - 150\cos v + 2\cos 2v + 2\cos V$ \quad $53\;\;50$ \quad $58\;\;50$
Ope priorum[?] ergo formularum ad momenta eclipsium tam solarium quam lunarinm facile definitur diameter lunae apparens et ejus parallaxis horizontalis: quoniam haec determinatio a sola anomalia lunae excentrica pendet, dum reliquae partes ab anomalia solis insuper pendentes tam fuerint exiguae, ut sine errore rejici queant.

§. 9. His expeditis investigationem motus lunae horarii suscipio: quae pariter ex aequatione differentiali, qua variatio longitudinis lunae momentanea $d\varphi$ continetur, est petenda. Quodsi vero ponamus anomaliam lunae mediam $=u$, excentricam $=v$, ut sit $du = dv\,(1 + k\cos v)$, distantiamque lunae a terra $=z$, erit $d\varphi = \frac{\alpha - \frac{3}{2}Mnn}{zz:cc}\,du$, existente
$\alpha = 1{,}0070234,\quad l\alpha = 0{,}0030396,\quad l\tfrac{3}{2}nn = 7{,}9312851$
Unde si $du$ denotet motum horarium anomaliae mediae, ut sit
$du = 32'\,39''\,48'''$,
valor differentialis $d\varphi$ dabit motum horarium lunae verum. Supra autem invenimus valorem litterae $M$ sequentem
$M = + A\cos 2\eta + Bk\cos(2\eta + v) + Ekk\cos 2(\eta - v) - Fe\cos(2\eta + V)$
$\quad + akk\cos 2\eta + Ck\cos(2\eta - v) - Ge\cos(2\eta - V)$
$\quad - Kke\cos(2\eta - v - V) + M\varepsilon\cos\eta + N\varepsilon\cos 3\eta + O\varepsilon k\cos(\eta - v)$
$\quad - Lke\cos(2\eta - v + V) - nnS\cos 4\eta + nnUk\cos v$

§. 10. Si jam pro his litteris valores supra inventos substituamus, reperiemus numeratorem fractionis $\alpha - \frac{3}{2}nnM =$
$1{,}0070234 + 0{,}004662\cos 2\eta + 0{,}0003385\cos(2\eta + v) + 0{,}0011281\cos(2\eta - v)$
$0{,}0030396 \quad 7{,}66857 \quad 6{,}529607 \quad 7{,}052357$
$-[?]\,0{,}0005506\cos(2\eta - 2v) - 0{,}0001170\cos(2\eta + V) - 0{,}0001269\cos(2\eta - V)$
$6{,}740834 \quad 6{,}068320 \quad 6{,}103616$
$+[?]\,0{,}0000364\cos(2\eta - v - V) - 0{,}0000293\cos(2\eta - v + V) + 0{,}0000084\cos\eta$
$5{,}560398 \quad 5{,}466904 \quad 4{,}921866$
$+[?]\,0{,}0000139\cos 3\eta - 0{,}0000124\cos(\eta - v) - 0{,}0000403\cos 4\eta + 0{,}0001987\cos v$
$5{,}143714 \quad 5{,}091308 \quad 5{,}6050 \quad 6{,}2981$
*

items.quote: quoniam haec determinatio a sola anomalia lunae excentrica pendet, dum reliquae partes ab anomalia solis insuper pendentes tam fuerint exiguae, ut sine errore rejici queant.
items.english: Since this determination depends only on the Moon's eccentric anomaly, while the remaining parts, which also depend on the Sun's anomaly, are so small that they can be rejected without error.

items.quote: His expeditis investigationem motus lunae horarii suscipio: quae pariter ex aequatione differentiali, qua variatio longitudinis lunae momentanea $d\varphi$ continetur, est petenda.
items.english: With these settled, I undertake the investigation of the Moon's hourly motion, which likewise must be obtained from the differential equation containing the instantaneous variation $d\varphi$ of the Moon's longitude.
